newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies steady.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies steady.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while early calls on pork belly futures were steady, livestock analysts said.

Expectations of another round of losses in cash hog prices on further numbers backed up by last week's storm and an easier tone to wholesale pork prices were expected to weigh on hog futures. Product demand eased late Monday, analysts said.
However, declines should again be curbed by a strong technical picture and the Taiwan pork ban which is expected to result in increased demand for U.S. pork from Japan, sources noted.

Expectations of a bullish CME Out-of-Town Report Tuesday afternoon was expected to support pork belly futures despite steady to lower cash belly quotes and larger-than-week-earlier hog slaughter on Monday. The narrowness of the premium of futures to the cash market likely kept storings very light last week, they said.
Estimates on the CME report ranged from unchanged to in 350,000 lbs versus in movement of 255,000 lbs last week and 1.99 million lbs moved into CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago last year.
